title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
dataset: ImageNet ImageNet-C OpenImage-O iWildCam Amazon CIFAR-10 CIFAR-100
main_contribution: generalized selective classification rejecting in-distribution label-shifted and covariate-shifted errors using two margin-based confidence scores requiring no training-data access
remaining_gap: no clinical data; no cross-hospital transfer; no frozen source-to-external threshold transfer; does not cross distribution shift with input availability
notes: full text viewed 2026-08-03; closest methodological neighbour; establishes selective-prediction-under-shift machinery in vision and NLP but does not take it to cross-institution clinical evaluation

title: Enhancing Chest X-ray Diagnosis with a Multimodal Deep Learning Network by Integrating Clinical History to Refine Attention
authors: Lian Yang and Yiliang Wan and Feng Pan
venue: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
dataset: MIMIC-CXR-JPG v2.0.0 single institution Beth Israel Deaconess
missingness_mechanism: image-masked and text-absent subsets not a controlled context intervention
main_contribution: MCX-Net fuses view-specific image encoders with clinical history through attention refinement; reports 135682 images with clinical history and a further 59846 without
remaining_gap: single institution with held-out splits only; no external hospital; no abstention or selective risk; no target-leakage audit of the text; no calibration or uncertainty transfer
notes: full text viewed 2026-08-03; closest clinical neighbour and a premise paper rather than a competitor; its 59846 images lacking clinical history is a natural-missingness observation not an intervention

title: Clinically-aligned Multi-modal Chest X-ray Classification (CaMCheX)
authors: Phillip Sloan and Edwin Simpson and Majid Mirmehdi
modalities: multi-view images, clinical indications and vital signs
external_validation: no - benchmark splits only, no second institution
missing_modality: partial - additive modality ablation during development, not an intervention on a fixed model
missingness_mechanism: components added cumulatively from a single-view baseline; contribution measured as the gain from each modality
selective_prediction: no - no abstention, rejection or confidence-thresholded evaluation appears in the full text
main_contribution: transformer fusion of multi-view radiographs with clinical indications and vital signs; the ablation reports 3.6 percent mAP from multi-view, a further gain from clinical indications, and 2.5 percent mAP from vital signs
remaining_gap: single-source benchmark evaluation with no second institution; the ablation measures what each modality adds during development rather than what a fixed model loses when context degrades at deployment; no abstention, no frozen threshold transfer, no leakage audit
notes: full text viewed 2026-08-07. Second premise paper alongside CW02: independently confirms clinical indications improve chest-radiograph classification. Its ablation is additive rather than interventional, so it establishes that context helps and not what its loss costs a deployed model

title: Missing-modality Enabled Multi-modal Fusion Architecture for Medical Data
authors: Muyu Wang and Shiyu Fan and Yichen Li and Zhongrang Xie and Hui Chen
venue: Journal of Biomedical Informatics vol 164 art 104796 (preprint arXiv 2309.15529)
missingness_mechanism: ablation applied to a single source; robustness is the objective rather than the estimand
main_contribution: transformer bi-modal fusion modules combined into a tri-modal framework with multivariate losses for robustness to missing modalities on a 14-label diagnosis task
remaining_gap: single source with held-out splits; treats missingness as a modelling problem to solve rather than an axis to measure; uses whole radiology reports rather than pre-diagnostic sections only; no abstention no threshold transfer no calibration across institutions
notes: arXiv abstract page viewed 2026-08-06; journal version paywalled; nearest work on the missing-modality axis and the clearest contrast with C3E which measures reliability under controlled context states instead of proposing a robust architecture

title: MoE-Health A Mixture of Experts Framework for Robust Multimodal Healthcare Prediction
authors: Xiaoyang Wang and Christopher C Yang
missingness_mechanism: varying availability handled architecturally; mechanism not stated in the abstract
main_contribution: mixture-of-experts selecting experts by available modality for mortality length-of-stay and readmission prediction
remaining_gap: single source; no chest-radiograph diagnosis task; no abstention; no cross-institution calibration or threshold transfer
notes: arXiv abstract page viewed 2026-08-06; adjacent on the missing-modality axis but a different clinical task

title: On the limits of cross-domain generalization in automated X-ray prediction
authors: Joseph Paul Cohen and Mohammad Hashir and Rupert Brooks and Hadrien Bertrand
main_contribution: argues cross-domain failure is driven by label shift rather than image shift; models with strong individual performance disagree substantially
remaining_gap: image-only with no clinical text; no selective prediction; no interaction between institution and context availability
notes: arXiv abstract page viewed 2026-08-06; foundational for the institution-shift axis alone and useful support for treating label source as consequential

title: CXR-LT 2026 Challenge Multi-Center Long-Tailed and Zero Shot Chest X-ray Classification
authors: Hexin Dong and Yi Lin and Pengyu Zhou and Fengnian Zhao and 24 others
dataset: PadChest and NIH Chest X-ray over 145000 images multi-center
main_contribution: multi-center long-tailed and zero-shot benchmark evaluating head-versus-tail performance calibration and cross-center generalization gaps
remaining_gap: names calibration and cross-center generalization as open problems, which supports rather than pre-empts the C3E gap; images only with radiologist annotations replacing report-derived labels; no context axis and no abstention
notes: arXiv abstract page viewed 2026-08-06; quotable evidence that cross-center calibration remains open as of 2026

title: Foundation Model Robustness to Technical Acquisition Parameters in Chest X-Ray AI: A Multi-Architecture Comparative Study with External Validation
dataset: RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge (n=26684) and NIH ChestX-ray14 (n=112120)
external_validation: partial - both datasets originate from the NIH Clinical Center so the contrast is principally a labelling-scheme shift rather than an institutional one
institution_shift: partial - labelling scheme rather than institution
selective_prediction: no - thresholds set per dataset by Youden J with no frozen transfer
calibration: yes - expected calibration error reported by view type on both datasets
main_contribution: compares four architectures for the sensitivity gap between AP and PA views; model rankings reverse completely on the second dataset. The domain-specific vision-language model degrades from a 14.3 percent gap to 48.9 percent while a self-supervised model stays near 25.2 to 22.3 percent
remaining_gap: images only with no pre-diagnostic clinical text; no abstention or selective risk; thresholds re-fitted per dataset rather than transferred frozen; the shift studied is acquisition view type and labelling convention rather than context availability
notes: full text viewed 2026-08-07. Supporting citation rather than a threat: it independently shows internal ranking failing to predict external ranking, the same class of failure C3E reports for a selective policy. Its own external contrast is same-institution with different labels, which sharpens rather than weakens the C3E cross-hospital claim
